update.evidence_span: HESA could be strengthened by the low stacking-fault energy of the matrix, high anti-phase boundary energy of the strengthening precipitate, and thermally stable microstructure
update.content: Low matrix stacking-fault energy, high precipitate APB energy, and microstructural stability strengthen HESA.

update.evidence_span: the creep curves of HESA were dominated by tertiary creep behavior
update.content: HESA creep is dominated by tertiary deformation.

update.evidence_span: the creep of HESA is dominated by parallel raft (P-raft) and without perpendicular γ/γ′ interfaces
update.content: Parallel rafting removes perpendicular gamma/gamma-prime interfaces during creep.

add.content: Prior studies inferred HEA creep mechanisms with nanoindentation.
add.evidence_span: some studies utilized nano-indentation method to deduce creep mechanism of HEA

add.content: Nanoindentation cannot include long-term microstructural stability.
add.evidence_span: these tests could not take the effect of long-term microstructure stability on creep into consideration

add.content: Earlier gamma-prime HEAs had lower solvus temperatures than conventional superalloys.
add.evidence_span: the γ′ solvus temperatures of the reported γ′-bearing HEAs still remained relatively low comparing to those of superalloys

add.content: HESA has a 1199 degrees C gamma-prime solvus and 69% precipitate fraction.
add.evidence_span: the γ′ solvus and solidus temperature are 1199 and 1276 °C, respectively

add.content: HESA creep activation energy is 290 kJ/mol versus 230 kJ/mol for CMSX-2.
add.evidence_span: the creep activation energy of HESA can be estimated to be 290 kJ/mol, while that of CMSX-2 is 230 kJ/mol

add.content: Dislocations bypass rather than shear gamma-prime precipitates during creep.
add.evidence_span: Instead, thermally activated by-passing of dislocations around γ′ precipitates should be the deformation mechanism

add.content: Parallel rafting explains the observed dominance of tertiary creep.
add.evidence_span: Tetzlaff et al . have reported that tertiary creep may dominate the creep response of P-rafted superalloys [47] , and this is exactly the creep behavior observed for HESA at 982 °C

add.content: Sluggish diffusion in the high-entropy matrix raises creep activation energy.
add.evidence_span: the sluggish diffusion of the high entropy γ matrix may have attributed to the higher creep activation energy
